title: Climbing Stairs
statement_short: You are climbing a staircase. It takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?
hint: Subproblem overlap (ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2)) dictates state memoization or space-optimized dynamic programming.
why_not: Right: 1D DP memoizes or tracks previous two step counts (ways[i] = ways[i-1] + ways[i-2]) in O(n) time and O(1) space. Not Backtracking: Exhaustive recursive search computes subproblems redundantly, causing TLE in O(2^n) time. Not Math / Geometry: Binet Fibonacci formula computes answer in O(log n), but 1D DP is the core subproblem memoization pattern. Not Greedy: Local step choices do not calculate global path count totals.
